PulseChain Arbitrum gateway withdrawals: historical execution
audit
Finding and scope
Historical execution traces were obtained for all 78 transactions containing the 106 withdrawals in
the existing event census. All 106 events match exactly one successful gateway finalization call by
gateway address, token address, recipient and raw amount. There are no trace-fetch failures, unmatched
events, trace identity mismatches or failed trace frames in this batch.
The executed paths comprise 104 transfer-only withdrawals, one ARB bridgeMint, and one GRT
mint followed by transfer. The GRT and ARB transactions remain the only demonstrated destination
issuance cases within this finite census. This extends the earlier receipt screen into complete historical
execution coverage; it does not establish completeness for other bridges, unidentified gateways,
different event signatures or later transactions.
The inherited fork boundary is block 17,232,999. The event interval is 17,233,000–27,659,393,
ending at block hash 0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275 on 28 September
2026 at 08:22:35 UTC. The event catalogues cover ten gateway addresses. Seven contain
withdrawals; HGOLD, WETH and the retired LPT gateway returned no matching withdrawals in the
preceding event searches and therefore provide no execution frames for this trace batch.
Executed gateway behavior
Gateway family Withdrawals Actual token calls used for
delivery
Standard ERC-20 93 93 transfer(recipient, amount) calls
Custom ERC-20 6 6 transfer(recipient, amount) calls
DAI 2 2 transferFrom(escrow, recipient,
amount) calls
wstETH 1 1 transfer(recipient, amount) call
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 136

Gateway family Withdrawals Actual token calls used for
delivery
LPT 1 1 transferFrom(escrow, recipient,
amount) call; no external minter call
ARB 1 1 bridgeMint(recipient, amount) call
GRT 2 2 transferFrom(escrow, recipient,
amount) calls; one also calls 
mint(escrow, shortfall)
The 105 transfer calls consist of 100 transfer calls and five transferFrom calls. Every one has recipient
and amount arguments exactly matching its withdrawal event. Of these calls, 103 return ABI-encoded 
true and two return empty data; none returns false. This establishes the calls, their successful execution
and matching declared amounts. Balance and supply reconciliation is a separate check, particularly for
tokens whose transfer semantics might differ from ordinary ERC-20 accounting.
The classification counts the initial call into a token once. An implementation delegatecall carrying the
same selector is not counted as a second transfer or mint. Calls elsewhere in a transaction are not
attributed to a gateway withdrawal merely because they occur in the same receipt.
Implementations observed during execution
These addresses come from the actual historical delegatecall frames, not from present-day proxy storage.
Each listed proxy used the same implementation throughout the withdrawals observed for that gateway
in this batch.
Gateway Implementation actually executed
Standard 0xa3a7b6f88361f48403514059f1f16c8e78d60eec 0xb4299a1f5f26ff6a98b7ba35572290c359fde900
Custom 0xcee284f754e854890e311e3280b767f80797180d 0xc8d26ab9e132c79140b3376a0ac7932e4680aa45
wstETH 0x0f25c1dc2a9922304f2eac71dca9b07e310e8e5a 0xc4e3ff0b5b106f88fc64c43031be8b076ee9f21c
ARB 0xbbce8aa77782f13d4202a230d978f361b011db27 0x4e8c24617c4592895d52ac6df29d9647e9d01bb5
GRT 0x01cdc91b0a9ba741903aa3699bf4ce31d6c5cc06 0xd41ca6a1d034d178c196dfa916f22f7d1a1b8222
DAI gateway 0xd3b5b60020504bc3489d6949d545893982ba3011 and LPT gateway 
0x6142f1c8bbf02e6a6bd074e8d564c9a5420a0676 execute directly in these transactions. This observation about
gateway execution does not mean that every downstream contract or token also executes directly.
Cases requiring more than a selector count
The GRT mint transaction contains both a mint and a transfer. Its mint is 
62,875,936.675361278837595998 GRT, while delivery is 62,875,937.675361278837595998
GRT. Existing escrow supplies the difference of one GRT. Counting the full delivery as minted would
overstate issuance. The separate GRT reconciliation (Appendix 12) contains the allowance, supply and
receipt evidence.
The January 2025 GRT withdrawal uses the same gateway implementation but calls only balanceOf and 
transferFrom on GRT. It contains no GRT mint call. The existence of a gateway's mint capability cannot
determine which funding branch a particular withdrawal actually used.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 137

The LPT withdrawal similarly calls balanceOf and transferFrom on LPT without calling its external minter. The
ARB withdrawal instead calls the exact destination token's bridgeMint, with no escrow transfer branch in
that execution.
T wo standard-gateway withdrawals, involving sUSD and SNX, contain an additional call back into the
token proxy with selector 0x907dff97. The proxies' verified ABIs identify this function as 
_emit(bytes,uint256,bytes32,bytes32,bytes32,bytes32). The recorded arguments specify the ERC-20 Transfer
event topic, the standard gateway as sender, the withdrawal recipient and the transferred amount.
These are token-proxy event emission calls, not additional mint calls. Their callers differ from the
gateway, and their positions are nested under the already identified transfer. Sources: sUSD proxy, SNX
proxy.
Reproduction and retained evidence
Run from the repository root:
python Research/scripts/audit_pulsechain_withdrawal_traces.py Research/experiments/
parb_withdrawal_trace_audit_20260929.json
The manifest names four existing event catalogues. It also identifies four retained historical traces for
reuse: ARB, LPT, the examined MIM withdrawal and the September GRT mint. The other 74 traces were
fetched using trace_transaction from https://rpc.pulsechain.com, with a maximum of four concurrent
requests. Existing trace files are reused on rerun. No transaction simulation, signing, state change or
transaction submission occurs.
Raw request/response records, source responses, event-level classifications and a SHA-256 evidence
manifest are retained under ignored artifacts/parb-withdrawal-trace-audit-20260929/. audit.json preserves
every event's gateway call path, exact-token calls, return data, gateway and token delegate targets,
transfer source and argument comparisons. Each trace frame's transaction hash, block number and
block hash is checked against the event. Error responses remain explicit errors rather than being
interpreted as empty traces or absence of activity.
These traces establish destination execution. They do not independently establish the corresponding
pARB source-chain transaction, source collateral or source-token burn. They also do not establish
subsequent use of the issued tokens as collateral or in purchases of pDAI; those are separate transaction
tracing questions.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 138
